newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close sharply lower, seen soft.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close sharply lower, seen soft.

text.p: Argentine stocks took a heavy hit Monday in token volume, dogged by lingering political worries in the aftermath of a corruption scandal sparked last week by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo.

"There's an overall negative trading environment," said Mariana Fabello at Banco Roberts. "There are still many political doubts and the fixed income market isn't taking off, which weighs on the bolsa."
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index slid 2.1 percent to 557.42. Last week the MerVal shed 2.5 percent, snapping a seven-week bull run.

"It's obvious that political tension has soured the mood and unleashed a wave of profit-taking," said Jose Napoli at brokers Ignoto y Napoli. "But I wouldn't say there's a whole lot of tension, especially considering the dismal volumes."
Floor turnover shrank to 10 million pesos from 17.5 million Friday, while over-the-counter volume halved to 62 million pesos.

Cavallo, who early last week accused two cabinet ministers of manipulating judges, was thronged by reporters Monday when he arrived in court to testify as a witness in a corruption probe involving Banco Nacion and the local unit of IBM.
"Nobody really knows what's happening with Cavallo, which is an important matter, so there's a lot of caution. We'll just have to wait and see," said Fabello.
Traders also noted last week's options expirations had drained the market's momentum.
"Options settlements were bulky and they came at a bad time, because those who sold positions are staying out of the market and strangling liquidity even more," said Napoli.
The bolsa's broad market index retreated 1.7 percent in the session, with losers pounding winners 39 to 5 and 15 issues closing flat.
All main-tier stocks posted losses in the session, except Bansud bank, construction stock Juan Minetti and power utility Capex, which closed unchanged.
The worst hit were construction company Polledo, which tumbled 6.0 percent, pulp and paper maker Celulosa and oil company Sol Petroleo, both off 5.9 percent.
